author: Mudassir Shabbir
summary: The 50-paper set includes 22 publications coauthored by Mudassir Shabbir on graph learning and its representation foundations, plus 28 influential papers selected for their significance to the field.
policy: Author coverage comes first: include the publicly verifiable graph-learning papers, graph descriptors, graph-learning applications, and directly relevant graph-distinguishability foundations coauthored by Mudassir Shabbir. Coverage was checked on 2 November 2026; this does not assert coverage of unpublished or unlisted manuscripts.

The remaining 28 readings are chosen for foundational ideas, influential model families, and established benchmarks or evaluation methods. This is a reasoned syllabus selection, not a citation-count ranking. It preserves PageRank, DeepWalk, node2vec, GCN, GAN, GAT and graph transformers, with message passing, self-supervision, and trustworthy evaluation.

A preprint and its published version count as one reading. Distinct conference and extended journal papers are retained where they make separate contributions; their relationship is noted. Preprints and works in progress are labeled. General geometry and control papers without a direct graph-learning contribution are outside this reading set.

All 50 receive class coverage through lectures, concise paper spotlights and discussions. The assigned week identifies the main discussion; groups may choose papers across weeks for their five-paper portfolio.

scope_notes: General computational geometry, graph controllability without learning, and general distributed optimization are not part of this graph machine learning inventory.
Pure cospectral enumeration and skew-walk-matrix papers are adjacent mathematical work; the directly relevant Control-based Conditions for Graph Distinguishability is included.

The 2026 Extracting Learning Backbones journal article is not counted as an author paper: the publisher lists Ahmad, Said, Koutsoukos and Abbas, without Shabbir, despite a conflicting coauthor webpage. The authored 2024-conference/2025-proceedings paper is included.

field_selection.title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web
field_selection.reason: Connects graph centrality, Markov chains, and ranking before learned representations.

field_selection.title: Laplacian Eigenmaps and Spectral Techniques for Embedding and Clustering
field_selection.reason: Introduces the graph Laplacian as a bridge between geometry, embeddings, and spectral learning.

field_selection.title: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
field_selection.reason: Turns short random walks into a practical unsupervised representation-learning pipeline.

field_selection.title: node2vec: Scalable Feature Learning for Networks
field_selection.reason: Shows how biased walks trade off local neighborhoods and structural roles.

field_selection.title: The Graph Neural Network Model
field_selection.reason: An early general formulation of neural computation on graphs; provides historical grounding for today’s message-passing architectures.

field_selection.title: Convolutional Neural Networks on Graphs with Fast Localized Spectral Filtering
field_selection.reason: Replaces expensive eigendecomposition with localized polynomial filters.

field_selection.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
field_selection.reason: Introduces neighborhood sampling and aggregation for generalization to unseen nodes.

field_selection.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
field_selection.reason: Unifies many graph architectures through message, update, and readout functions.

field_selection.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
field_selection.reason: Establishes a compact, reproducible baseline for learning from node features and edges.

field_selection.title: Graph Attention Networks
field_selection.reason: Introduces learned neighborhood weighting and multi-head attention.

field_selection.title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Differentiable Pooling
field_selection.reason: Introduces learned graph coarsening for prediction over entire graphs.

field_selection.title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
field_selection.reason: Relates aggregation to graph isomorphism and motivates the Graph Isomorphism Network.

field_selection.title: Beyond Homophily in Graph Neural Networks: Current Limitations and Effective Designs
field_selection.reason: Studies graphs whose connected nodes differ and motivates separating ego and neighbor information.

field_selection.title: On the Bottleneck of Graph Neural Networks and its Practical Implications
field_selection.reason: Introduces over-squashing as a failure of information transmission across graph bottlenecks.

field_selection.title: Deep Graph Infomax
field_selection.reason: Introduces node representation learning through local-global contrast.

field_selection.title: Graph Contrastive Learning with Augmentations
field_selection.reason: Makes graph augmentations a central design choice in contrastive pretraining.

field_selection.title: GraphSAINT: Graph Sampling Based Inductive Learning Method
field_selection.reason: Studies subgraph sampling with normalization to improve training efficiency.

field_selection.title: Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks
field_selection.reason: Extends message passing to typed relations and knowledge-graph completion.

field_selection.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
field_selection.reason: Introduces temporal attention with continuous-time encodings.

field_selection.title: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?
field_selection.reason: Shows how structural encodings make global attention useful for graph prediction.

field_selection.title: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer
field_selection.reason: Combines local message passing, global attention, and position or structure encodings.

field_selection.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
field_selection.reason: Provides the adversarial-learning prerequisite; this paper itself is not a graph model.

field_selection.title: GraphGAN: Graph Representation Learning with Generative Adversarial Nets
field_selection.reason: Applies adversarial training to connectivity distributions for graph embeddings.

field_selection.title: GraphRNN: Generating Realistic Graphs with Deep Auto-regressive Models
field_selection.reason: Provides an autoregressive alternative to adversarial graph generation.

field_selection.title: MolGAN: An implicit generative model for small molecular graphs
field_selection.reason: Combines adversarial graph generation with property objectives and exposes mode collapse.

field_selection.title: Adversarial Attacks on Graph Neural Networks via Meta Learning
field_selection.reason: Studies sensitivity to training-graph perturbations and motivates robust evaluation.

field_selection.title: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
field_selection.reason: Explores which subgraphs and features support a GNN prediction.

field_selection.title: Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs
field_selection.reason: Supplies task-specific datasets, realistic splits, and standardized evaluators.
